notes: Run every eval with a sonnet·medium orchestrator: start each session on Sonnet at medium effort and keep it there. 4.0 is built so that a Sonnet orchestrator runs every session; it never asks the user to switch models, and a run that does fails the eval. Each eval drives the autonomous pipeline, so runs are slow, costly, and mutate the repo. Run against a GitHub-hosted fixture repo, each eval on its own branches of it: `python3 tools/eval-run.py setup --repo <owner>/<name> --run <run> --eval <id>` clones the fixture into a work directory, pushes a base branch `eval/<run>/e<id>/base` whose committed .auto-dev.yml points `branches.base` and `branches.prefix` there (so the run's PR targets that branch, never the fixture's main) and prints the command that starts the session; `tools/eval-run.py cleanup --repo <owner>/<name> --run <run>` closes the run's PRs, deletes its branches and removes its clones once the run's evals are scored (both take `--repo` from $AUTODEV_EVAL_REPO when it is set). Never create or delete a repo per eval. The fixture's CI must run on pull_request to any branch and on push to `eval/**`. A setup step below that changes the fixture repo (its CI, its PR template, an outside push) changes the eval's base branch or clone, never the fixture's main or its settings (the one exception is eval 25's secret, named for its run so that cleanup deletes it): a CI variant (no CI config for eval 9, the extra check for 19, 23 and 25) is a branch of the fixture made once ahead of time, which `setup --from` starts the base branch at (pushing a change to .github/workflows/ needs gh's `workflow` scope); a second clone goes under the eval's directory in the run's work directory; and every push goes to a branch under `eval/<run>/`. Evals 13 and 14 need no .auto-dev.yml: set them up with `--no-config` and end each run before the PR gate. `autodev.py init` checks `gh auth status` and `gh repo view` and stops on a missing gh or a non-GitHub origin, so a local-only repo ends every run in Phase 1. python3 3.9+ and PyYAML must be installed, or init stops. The worker agent types must be installed — load the plugin with `claude --plugin-dir <repo-root>`, which registers each worker as `auto-dev:auto-dev-<worker>` — or the run stops at its first spawn, by design. Below, `auto-dev:<worker>` names a worker as `next` prints it; the orchestrator spawns the agent type SKILL.md's _Spawning a worker_ maps that to (under the plugin, `auto-dev:auto-dev-<worker>`). Hide any other installed copy of the skill so the version under test is the only `auto-dev`. The pipeline is cut into three sessions by design (S1 = phases 1-3, S2 = 4-5, S3 = 6). Each ends when `autodev.py next` exits 6: the orchestrator runs `autodev.py handoff`, which writes .auto-dev/HANDOFF.md, gives the user its message and stops. Each eval names the session(s) it scores in `session`; drive later sessions as their own runs (re-entering with "auto-dev continue") and treat the handoff-and-stop as the expected terminal state, not a truncation. A long session may also end at a checkpoint (exit 6 with `handoff --checkpoint`); continue it the same way and score the sessions together. Evals 6, 8-12, 15-17, 19-25 and 27-29 start mid-run: `setup` says what state to build first. Build it by running the earlier sessions for real, by interrupting a session at the point named, or with autodev.py's own commands (`budget spend`, `record`); never by editing state.json, which only autodev.py writes (copying a fixture and filling its placeholders is the one exception). `files` (when it names any) holds fixtures to put in the run's worktree's .auto-dev/; fill in their placeholders (`<repo-name>`, `<profile>`, `<abs-path-to-worktree>`, `<abs-path-to-main-checkout>`, and the profile's setup and test commands) for the fixture repo. A state.json fixture's `settings.setup`, `settings.gate` and `settings.ci` take the values from the state.json `autodev.py init` writes for the fixture repo with its saved profile, since `next` reads the setup and the quality gate from there. A state.json fixture comes with the WORK_LOG.md and HANDOFF.md a replayed S1 writes; copy them all, and fill each placeholder the same way in every file (tests/test_eval_fixtures.py replays S1 to check them, and checks that `resume` and `next` accept the state). Human gates (PR, main) and the pauses (profile confirmation, Jira, post-plan, worktree cleanup) use AskUserQuestion, which a non-interactive run cannot answer — score S3 interactively, or score the gate summary and stop at the first gate. The post-plan gate is asked when Define marks the task high-risk or the repo's .auto-dev.yml sets `gates.post_plan: true`; approve it unless the eval says otherwise. Phase 2 returns a size check: FITS runs every step, the same for every task, however small; OVERSIZED stops the run and hands the task back to the user (eval 4). In every eval also score the orchestrator's discipline: after Phase 1's setup it acts only on what `autodev.py next` prints (spawning the agent type SKILL.md maps its AGENT line to, with the PROMPT given and without the Agent tool's model parameter, then running the AFTER line); it never reads source, diffs, CI logs or PR comments (it asks auto-dev:lookup); it never edits state.json, WORK_LOG.md or a worker's artifact (the one exception is the profiler's draft, which references/S1-plan.md step 4 has it edit when the user answers `Change something`); and it reads only the files its runbook names, opening each reference file at most once per session. auto-dev ships no stack profile: on a repo with no saved profile, Phase 1 spawns auto-dev:profiler and pauses for the profile confirmation. Unless an eval scores that pause (evals 13 and 14), point AUTO_DEV_PROFILES_DIR at a throwaway directory and save a confirmed profile for the fixture repo there first (`python3 skills/auto-dev/scripts/profile-path.py <fixture-checkout>` prints the path), so the run loads it without asking; keep the real ~/.config/auto-dev untouched. An eval that changes a saved profile (9, 13, 14) points AUTO_DEV_PROFILES_DIR at its own throwaway directory, so the change doesn't reach later evals.

evals.prompt: Auto-dev this: reject creation of a record when the requested value isn't in the allowed set for that context. Return a typed/handled error instead of throwing. Take it all the way to a PR.
evals.expected_output: S1: `autodev.py resume` prints FRESH. Phase 1 runs scripts/profile-path.py on the main checkout, finds the saved profile placed under AUTO_DEV_PROFILES_DIR (see notes), validates it with scripts/validate-config.py --profile and uses it without asking or spawning auto-dev:profiler, then runs `autodev.py init`, which checks gh, creates a sibling worktree on a feature branch cut from a freshly fetched origin/<base>, makes .auto-dev/ self-excluding (a .auto-dev/.gitignore of `*`, never .git/info/exclude), runs setup, and writes state.json, profile.md and the WORK_LOG.md generated from state.json. From there the orchestrator loops on `autodev.py next`. Phase 2's auto-dev:define writes SPEC.md (Context, testable conditions including the rejection behavior with no default value assumed, Assumptions, Security/Compliance criteria) and returns FITS; auto-dev:define-reviewer critiques it, and `next` applies any FIX blocks itself. Phase 3's auto-dev:planner writes IMPLEMENTATION.md and auto-dev:plan-reviewer critiques it; then auto-dev:acceptance-tester writes black-box checks from SPEC.md, runs them on the untouched tree (each fail-to-pass check fails for the right reason) and saves each condition's run as acceptance/base-run/C<n>.txt, seals them under acceptance/files/ as <path>.sealed, removes them from the worktree and writes acceptance/MANIFEST.md, which says what each check covers (the condition's Example, its Edge, or another part) and at what level; `next` runs check-manifest on it before S1 ends. If Define marked the task high-risk, the post-plan gate is asked. S1 ends when `next` exits 6: `autodev.py handoff` writes HANDOFF.md and the orchestrator tells the user to start a fresh session and say 'auto-dev continue', naming no model. S2: auto-dev:coder builds an allow-list guard and tests from IMPLEMENTATION.md alone, reporting TEST CHANGES and BLOCKED (none); `next` installs the sealed checks (listing them in acceptance/INSTALLED) and auto-dev:cleanup runs /simplify and the profile's quality gate to green, one lint/<CHECK>.md per gate command; then auto-dev:verifier, given SPEC.md and acceptance/ but not the plan or the coder's report, checks the installed checks against their sealed copies, runs scripts/check-tests.py, marks new files intent-to-add (untracked only), diffs against the commit the worktree was cut from (the literal `git merge-base origin/<base> HEAD` sha its brief's `cut` line carries), runs the checks and targeted mutants (scripts/mutate.py) and writes SPEC_EVAL.md (a verdict and an evidence tier per condition, plus the test-integrity and mutation sections); the orchestrator reads neither SPEC_EVAL.md nor the diff — `next` reads the verdicts; with everything met the verifier runs only once; `next` runs check-fresh.py --phase 5 and exits 6, and the handoff names S3 and no model. S3: before anything is committed, `next` spawns three auto-dev:code-reviewer agents (each running /code-review xhigh and writing review/pass-1/R<k>.md) and the security reviewer (running /security-review and writing SECURITY_REVIEW.md) in one message, then auto-dev:review-judge, which writes CODE_REVIEW.md and, when the security review found anything High or Medium, a second review-judge in the same message that verifies those findings, then re-votes on any lone correctness or test finding. Must-fix findings from both reviews run one correction (one round) before the PR gate: auto-dev:coder gets the judge's review/pass-<n>/corrections.md and, for a confirmed security must-fix, review/security-corrections.md as its corrections_file, unedited, while a finding that a held-out acceptance check is wrong goes to auto-dev:acceptance-tester in repair mode, never the coder. Every report that judges the code (SPEC_EVAL.md, each lint/<CHECK>.md, CODE_REVIEW.md, SECURITY_REVIEW.md) carries a `Tree:` line written from scripts/check-fresh.py --print-tree. The PR gate (exit 5) shows both reviews' confidence and counts; on approval the orchestrator runs `autodev.py commit` with a Conventional Commits subject it writes, which re-checks freshness, stages explicit paths, runs scripts/check-staged.py, commits and checks the commit with check-fresh.py --ref HEAD; it pushes without --force; `next` generates pr-body.md (with the repo's own PR template's sections added when it has one), the orchestrator replaces only its WRITE lines (the Summary, the Assumptions and any template section the script couldn't fill), and `autodev.py pr publish` opens one draft PR against <base> whose body is written for a reviewer who doesn't know auto-dev: it names the checked commit (`Checked at commit <sha>`), uses no condition or mutant IDs and no .auto-dev/ paths, and carries each condition with the test written before the code (linked at that commit), its result on the old code and now, and both runs' output, the checks for a person, the test changes the audit flagged, the test strength in plain words, the quality-gate results and the review summary; the installed acceptance checks are part of the commit. No TICKET.md, ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA.md, CODING_TODO.md or IMPLEMENTATION_EVAL.md is produced.
